The 0.11.1 token read returns fewer than 1000 rows or loses the known-present power_convertor control, catching an instrument that sees nothing.
A mapped row's new token spelling is missing from the 0.11.1 token set; it reads the graph independently of the mapping file, so a dropped grammar row reddens it.
The source is already claimed, the retry reports anything but one retried source, or the compose hint reports not applied; each reads a writer's returned receipt rather than the input.
More than one SNRun names the focus manifest, which would make run-scoped cost attribution ambiguous.

Any of the four parked sources changes status or captured state; it compares the live after-snapshot to the independently captured mapping-before.json, so a stray write or a newly resolvable token reddens it.

findings.text: non-blocking: the parked-source table carries the recorded 0.11.0-era refusal text as the only statement about the token, and never reports the per-source answer the done_when names - whether ISN 0.11.1 now carries it, read from the active grammar. The run script computes the 0.11.1 token set at lines 95-102 and applies it only to admitted mapping rows, so mapping-before.json holds no presence record for the four parked tokens. The node's conclusion is nevertheless correct: an independent read of the active grammar version 0.11.1 returns one physical_base row for current_profile_alignment, two rows for the power_convertor positive control, and zero rows for plasma_current_element_thick_line, electron_cyclotron_power_deposition_peak, ion_cyclotron_power_deposition_peak and lower_hybrid_power_deposition_peak. Record that query and its four zero counts in the fragment so the parked verdict rests on a measurement rather than on the stored refusal.

non-blocking: render() re-asserts on result['own_names'] the same two predicates that built that list at lines 262-268 (a generate_name phase in own_phases, and created_at at or after run started_at), so both assertions are tautologies that cannot redden whatever the pipeline did. The attribution guard that does work is the filter itself, and nothing asserts it; the assertions that carry real weight are the parkled-state equality at line 251, the spend ceiling at line 253 and the armed-grammar check at lines 58 and 99.

non-blocking: the summary field parked_controls_unchanged is len(payload['parked']), a constant 4 that counts the controls examined rather than measuring that any is unchanged; the measurement is the equality assertion at line 251, which aborts the run before this field is written. A reader who quotes the field as the check is quoting the input set, so name it parked_controls_asserted or carry the comparison's own count.
